title: F-16A Block 10/15 — Stability & Control vs Ground Truth
condition: Run at Brandt's own W_TO=31377.00 lbf, W_energy=6296.30 lbf (Wt!B3/B38, Wt!B6), cruise Mach 0.87 (f16a_requirements.json, DI-reused via weights.cruise_mach).
referenceDesc: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_stability_control_ground_truth.json (neutral_point, cg_takeoff, cg_landing, CLa_aircraft, CLa_per_surface, aero_center) -- Brandt-F16-A.xls, sheet 'S&C (2)'.
secondDesc: Roskam Eqns 3.17/3.19/3.24/3.38 (Brandt's OWN cited source for CLa/neutral point) -- NOT this repo's toolbox formula, and NOT in this repo at all (that specific Roskam title, "Airplane Flight Dynamics and Automatic Flight Controls, Part I," is not extracted anywhere here); cited only as the explanation for the headline finding.

rows.parameter: [CENTER OF GRAVITY x_cg -- weighted-average identity, level-agnostic]

rows.notes: Run at Brandt's own W_TO/W_energy operating point. This framework's x_cg is built from a DIFFERENT component-weight/x-station table (this framework's own 10 WeightsL2 groups, re-aggregated from the legacy temp_Casey 22-row sheet -- docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md "Component-x-location buildup") than Brandt's own internal CG closure, so an exact match is not expected; this row checks whether the two land in the same physical neighborhood.
Same component-x-station table as L2 (cg_x_ft is fidelity-independent per the input JSON's own note) -- expect the same %Diff as the L2 row above.

rows.parameter: [AERODYNAMIC CENTERS x_acw / x_ach -- Eq. 16.12 (wing) and quarter-MAC (tail, no Mach term)]

rows.notes: Framework value includes Eq. 16.12's Mach-shift term evaluated at the real cruise Mach (0.87, in the 0.4<=M<=1.1 transonic-shift regime); Brandt's own simplified xacW value appears to omit this shift (F16SandCL3.md's own hand-check, done at M<0.4 where the shift is exactly 0, landed within +0.01% of Brandt -- the REMAINING gap at the real M=0.87 is almost entirely this shift term, not a wing-geometry wiring error). A small, EXPLAINED gap is expected here, not an exact match.
No Mach-shift term applied to the tail (documented simplification -- Raymer gives no Eq. 16.12-style correction for a tail surface, see SandCL3.x_ac_surface's own header).

rows.parameter: [LIFT-CURVE SLOPES -- linked to F16AeroL3.get_CL_alpha / SandCL3.CL_alpha_h, NOT re-derived]

rows.cite: Brandt-F16-A.xls, sheet S&C (2), row 24 (CLaW), in-sheet cite Roskam Eqn 3.24
rows.notes: [ROOT CAUSE, see headline finding above] Framework: Raymer Eq. 12.6/12.8 (F16AeroL3.get_CL_alpha). Brandt: Roskam Eqn 3.24 -- a DIFFERENT textbook method this repo cannot cross-check (that Roskam title is not in this repo). The ~23% gap here plausibly explains most of the x_np/SM divergence reported below, since Xnp_bar is a weighted blend dominated by this ratio.
Framework: SandCL3.CL_alpha_h, reusing AeroL2.CL_alpha a second time with the HT's own AR/sweep (same Raymer Eq. 12.6/12.8 family as the wing row above, same root-cause caveat).

rows.parameter: CLa, aircraft (Roskam Eq. 3.24 aggregate) -- NOT MODELED
rows.notes: This framework has no single "aircraft CL_alpha" quantity analogous to Roskam Eq. 3.24's aggregate -- Eqs. 16.8/16.9 combine CL_alpha_wing/CL_alpha_tail directly inside the Cm_alpha/neutral-point sum instead of forming an intermediate aircraft-level slope. Recorded as NOT MODELED, not a %Diff to chase.

rows.parameter: [NEUTRAL POINT x_np AND STATIC MARGIN SM -- THE HEADLINE FINDING]

rows.cite: Brandt-F16-A.xls, sheet S&C (2), row 33 (xnp), in-sheet cite Roskam Eqn 3.38
rows.notes: Framework: Raymer Eq. 16.9 (power-off, thrust term dropped per Raymer's own p.593 sanction). Brandt: Roskam Eqn 3.38, itself built on Roskam's own CLa/CLaHS (Eqns 3.17/3.19/3.24, a different textbook method this repo cannot cross-check -- see the [ROOT CAUSE] CL_alpha rows above and docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md's "Major new lead" section for the full record). This gap is a real, already-diagnosed, cross-textbook-method divergence, NOT a bug -- no input/citation is adjusted here to force closer agreement.

rows.cite: Brandt-F16-A.xls, sheet S&C (2), row 37 (SM, takeoff loading)
rows.notes: Framework computes SM ~ +0.18 (comfortably stable) at this operating point vs Brandt's SM_TO ~ -0.0022 (essentially neutral, very slightly unstable at takeoff loading) -- same root cause as the x_np row above (the ~23% CL_alpha gap dominates), COMPOUNDED by the different x_cg table (see the x_cg rows above). Both factors push in the SAME direction here.
